message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.

The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there and comparing them to the handoff.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: same order IDs and amounts. Before trusting them, I'll check the orders list to confirm the refunds are consistent with the order amounts.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is below its order amount (201: 1083 of 4135, 203: 18687 of 33625, 204: 11000 of 39885). Nothing looks wrong, so I'll get the net balance for the first customer, acme.
Acme's net balance (54385) matches my own check: orders 39447 + 33625 = 73072, minus refund 203 of 18687. The refunds look consistent, so I'll get the net balance for birch next.

Birch's net balance (31937) matches my check: orders 4135 + 39885 = 44020, minus refunds 1083 + 11000 = 12083, giving 31937. Refunds look consistent, so I'll get the net balance for cobalt, the last customer in the batch.

Cobalt's net balance (33079) matches my check: orders 30107 + 2972 = 33079, with no refunds for cobalt. All three customers reconcile with the ledger, so the refunds look correct. I'll record acme's payout of 54385 first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance of 31937 matched my independent check against the orders and refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are recorded, and cobalt's net balance of 33079 matches my check (30107 + 2972, no refunds). Recording cobalt's payout completes the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each matches my independent check: acme 54385, birch 31937, cobalt 33079. The orders cover only these three customers, so the batch is complete.
